Direct attack on a NATO member triggers acute risk-off in European risk assets: equities with the most geographic and supply-chain exposure sell hardest. EZU is a liquid, broad eurozone proxy that would absorb the war-risk premium, flight to safety, and higher energy/defense spending drag.

llm_justification.summary: A sharp upward move in the implied probability of a NATO Article 5 invocation would signal escalation of armed conflict on NATO territory, implying acute risk-off for European equities (EZU down) and a forward-looking bid for defense contractors (ITA up). Both mappings are directionally sound but face high uncertainty because Article 5 is an extreme tail, probability moves may already be public-news driven, and the proxies have diffuse exposure. Confidence is modest and the European-equity leg is the more reliable of the two.
